import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/dogs_zurich.csv')

# Filter for the latest available year to get a snapshot of the most current data
latest_year = df['StichtagDatJahr'].max()
df_latest = df[df['StichtagDatJahr'] == latest_year].copy() # Use .copy() to avoid SettingWithCopyWarning

# Prepare the 'AlterVHundLang' column for ordered plotting
# Get unique age groups and their corresponding sort values from 'AlterVHundSort'
# This ensures age groups are displayed in a logical order (e.g., 0-Jährige, 1-Jährige, ..., 10+-Jährige)
age_order_df = df_latest[['AlterVHundLang', 'AlterVHundSort']].drop_duplicates().sort_values('AlterVHundSort')
age_order = age_order_df['AlterVHundLang'].tolist()

# Set the aesthetic style of the plots
sns.set_style("whitegrid")

# Create a figure and axes for the plot
plt.figure(figsize=(14, 8)) # Set a larger figure size for better readability

# Create a countplot to visualize the distribution of dog age groups, separated by gender
# Using 'AlterVHundLang' on the x-axis and 'SexHundLang' as hue for gender separation
# The 'order' parameter ensures the age groups are displayed correctly
sns.countplot(
    data=df_latest,
    x='AlterVHundLang',
    hue='SexHundLang',
    order=age_order,
    palette='viridis', # A perceptually uniform colormap
    edgecolor='black' # Add edge color for better bar separation
)

# Add a descriptive title to the plot
plt.title(
    f'Distribution of Dog Age Groups by Gender in Zurich ({latest_year})',
    fontsize=18,
    pad=20 # Add padding to the title
)

# Label the x-axis
plt.xlabel('Dog Age Group', fontsize=14, labelpad=10)
# Rotate x-axis labels for better readability, especially with longer labels
plt.xticks(rotation=45, ha='right', fontsize=11)

# Label the y-axis
plt.ylabel('Number of Dogs', fontsize=14, labelpad=10)
plt.yticks(fontsize=11)

# Add a legend to distinguish between dog genders
plt.legend(
    title='Dog Gender',
    title_fontsize='13',
    fontsize='11',
    loc='upper right', # Position the legend
    frameon=True, # Show a frame around the legend
    edgecolor='black'
)

# Add a subtle grid for easier value estimation
plt.grid(axis='y', linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)

# Adjust plot layout to prevent labels from overlapping
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure to a file
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
